rationale: Cod hydrolysate exercise testing found inconclusive time to exhaustion. Clinical Parkinson fatigue was measured against overall diet, with no grilled cod estimate.
Pineapple was one component of a Parkinson diet reporting only aggregate motor change. Injected bromelain improved rat motor proxies after pretreatment. No raw pineapple hand dexterity estimate.
The Parkinson diet included cantaloupe and a composite scale containing rest tremor. No item-level change, raw preparation or cantaloupe-specific comparison.
Plum extract cell survival differed by toxin and bench levodopa darkening does not measure drug availability or dyskinesia. The Parkinson menu did not test poached plum or measure dyskinesia.
A Parkinson smell test included fish scent as a stimulus. The paper did not identify cod or test smell after eating baked cod.
Healthy-adult Extramel studies reported improved fatigue measures. Other melon concentrate or gliadin trials were inconclusive. No study tested raw cantaloupe for Parkinson fatigue.
A cod hydrolysate trial in older adults found inconclusive grip effects. No study tested grilled cod against Parkinson micrographia.

Bladder pain surveys reported pineapple-related worsening. A case-crossover gave inconclusive flare odds for a pooled fruit or juice item. Neither design measured raw pineapple and urgency episodes in Parkinson.
